In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mice have been a crucial model for understanding prion and neurodegenerative diseases.
prion disease research has been a major driving force behind the development of new and more powerful mouse models of other neurodegenerative diseases, which has been of great benefit for the field.
the use of mice as an experimental model for neurodegenerative disease is not a substitute for the use of other species, but a complement to the study of the disease in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have learned that prion diseases in mice and in humans are not caused by an infectious agent but by a conformational change of a host-encoded protein, the prion protein.
the study of prion diseases in mice has been instrumental in understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
the study of prion diseases in mice has led to an understanding of the fundamental mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of these diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of prion disease, mice have proven to be a powerful model for understanding the mechanisms of prion propagation and transmission and for identifying new therapeutic strategies.
mice have been and continue to be a powerful tool for understanding the mechanisms and causes of neurodegeneration in humans.
, despite the differences between the neurodegenerative disease models, the underlying molecular and cellular processes that drive disease are similar.
